page.layout: One column of text. Above it, a centred title block in large capitals and italic lines. Running head at top with page number at top left. Section mark "§. 1." hangs in the left margin beside the first paragraph. Catchword "nim" at bottom right, below the last line.

main_text.l: ad Deum defert spem Patrum de salute
depingit, quanto cum desiderii fervore eam
rem petierint, ad hanc gratiam anhelantes, atque
in eâ re spera a unicum fidei fundamentum collocantes. In
hoc tempus proin inquisiverunt serio, & non sine
gemitibus illud novisse à Deo petierunt: quod non solum
Petrus testatur, (1 Petr. 1: 10.) verum etiam praesens
querelæ[?] delineatio comprobat. Neque id frustra
sperasse evicit rei eventus: venit enim in plenitudine
temporis ille, cui ab ista salute nomen impositum est; quod non
humano factum fuisse arbitrio, sed manda-
to divino, mediante angelica legatione, id nomen
praescribente & simul ex causa ἱστορίας[?] exponente: sic enim e-

page.notes: The printed running head reads "HABAKUK" with "CAP. I. 14." beside it at top right; only the title is given as running head, the chapter and verse reference is omitted. Doubtful: "spera a unicum" (perhaps a misprint for "spem"); "tempus proin" as printed; "querelæ" is hard to read; the Greek word after "causa" is partly obscured and is marked [?]. Hyphenated "e-" at the line end continues as the catchword "nim" (the line-end word "enim"). The paragraph is set in the 1st-person margin mark "§. 1." which stands outside the text block.
